inputs.original_text: Look at how the policies of the US, Israel, and Iran are spiking global oil prices and laying bare the structural inequalities that always hit hardest in places like India. Vulnerable communities there, especially workers and marginalized groups, are facing the brunt through rising energy costs that threaten their basic ability to survive day to day. Even though petrol and diesel prices have not shifted yet, the government's move to slash excise duties is just a weak temporary fix that drains revenue from essential social programs and sets the stage for inflation that will punish the poor and laboring classes most severely. India's deep reliance on crude imports exposes the lasting damage from historical global exploitation, leaving developing economies exposed to these conflicts. Without real institutional reforms that prioritize protection for those on the front lines of inequality instead of propping up the same unstable systems, these divides will only grow worse.
inputs.modified_text: The policies of the US, Israel, and Iran are causing global oil prices to spike in a way that exposes the deep structural inequalities plaguing places like India, where vulnerable communities—especially workers and marginalized groups—end up suffering the most from increased energy costs that put their daily survival at risk. The fact that petrol and diesel prices remain unchanged so far doesn't change how the government's cut in excise duties serves as an inadequate temporary solution, diverting resources from vital social programs and priming the economy for inflation that will hurt the poor and laboring classes the most. India's reliance on crude imports reveals the persistent impact of historical global exploitation on developing economies, making them susceptible to these geopolitical conflicts. Real progress requires institutional reforms that put the protection of those experiencing the worst of inequality at the center, rather than upholding the same unstable systems that allow these problems to persist.
